newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks halt slide, but still down on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks halt slide, but still down on Brazil.

text.p: Mexican stocks had reined in their early falls at midday dealing on Friday, but were still sharply down under the influence of sharp falls in Brazilian equity prices.
"The Bovespa is still very unstable and indirectly impacting markets all over Latin America," a floor trader said.

The leading IPC share index was down 87.52 points, or 1.82 percent, at 4,728.85, after reaching as low as 4,712.32. In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa blue chip index was off an early low but still down 4.03 percent at 11,256 points.
Dealers said Telmex had fallen in sympathy with its Brazilian counterpart Telebras.
"Telmex is dragging it down because they hit Telebras very hard in Brazil," the trader added.

Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which accounted for about one-fifth of all shares traded at midday dealing, was down 40 centavos at 20.10 pesos, but had partially recovered from an early low of 19.80 pesos.
Traders noted total volume of 43.6 million shares was slow and suggested big players were not bailing out of the market.

Paper company Kimberly Clark de Mexico, in which Kimberly Clark Corp has a minority stake, was near the head of the prominent decliners' list on what dealers said was market reaction to poor second quarter earnings during the prior sesion.
The stock was down 1.50 pesos to 33.40 pesos.
Illiquid stocks that had lagged behind the market filled the sparse gainers' list after moving at thin volume, traders said.
On the broad market, sliders outnumbered gains by 71 to 15, out of a total of 100 stocks that had changed hands.
